name: ACP PaymentManager releasePayment double release
summary: PaymentManager.releasePayment had its escrow check commented out and recorded the claim only on an in-memory copy of the job, so each call paid the full budget again from pooled escrow. The attacker created a 97,000 USDC job with its own provider, completed it and called claimBudget to release it twice; copycats re-claimed other completed jobs.
notes: Anchored on the first unaffiliated exploit. EOA 0x7346dc42102b5cdba321d587564612d1f3878ad2 is the protocol's claim keeper (about 690k claimBudget calls on both ACP versions since July 2025, no proceeds of its own); its 1,869 re-releases from block 37590595 paid job providers, evaluators and the treasury, so they are affiliated (rule 5) and not in campaign or loss (about $2.9k).

PaymentManager is the only target: the fix (0x536823c8, block 42834676) restored its escrow check, while ACPRouter's claim path is unchanged across its upgrades, including those earlier on 2026-03-02, and holds no claim state. Its 2026-01 treasury and fee change only redirects fees.

Gross USDC that PaymentManager paid out in second releases (provider, evaluator and platform fees), at loss.mjs prices; the attacker's own 97,000 USDC budget funded the first release in the same transaction and nets out.
